lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Sam has put this bowl through the dishwasher twice. It still looks like dinner is in progress.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: You had one job.

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: And you gave me an obstacle course.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Two charges. Wasting water. Failing to wash. How do you plead?

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: I'd like to question the loader.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Sam bought a machine to get out of washing dishes. Now he's doing it before the cycle and after. Tonight, he's demanding a refund.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The dishwasher requests footage from last night. Sam stands at the sink, rinsing a plate. Then another. The faucet keeps running. By the time each plate enters the machine, Sam has practically washed it.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: I'm helping.

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: You hired a dishwasher and then did its shift.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: I thought I had to get the food off first.

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: Big scraps, yes. The actual washing was my part. Check my instructions. We have a whole section on this.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: A document this court suspects has never been opened.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: You run for hours. How is that saving water?

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: Because I'm not a faucet running for hours. Water collects at the bottom. A pump sends it through the spray arms. The water entering those arms is filtered. Hot water, detergent, and moving jets do the cleaning. Later, the dirty water drains away and fresh water rinses the dishes.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The court watches a cutaway. This machine doesn't fill to the roof like a bathtub. And rinsing every plate at the sink adds water use before its cycle even starts.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: Fine. Then explain the dirty bowl.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The rack rolls forward. Two bowls are tucked tightly together. The dirty one is hiding inside the other.

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: How was the spray supposed to reach that surface?

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: I was saving space.

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: You also saved that bowl from being washed.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Sam separates them. For the first time, the inside of the bowl has an open path toward the spray.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: And the obstacle course?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: With the machine off, Sam gently turns the lower spray arm. It bumps into a long utensil hanging below the rack. Sam moves it. The arm turns freely.

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: That thing is supposed to move. You gave it a parking brake.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The dishwasher looks ready to collect damages. Then Sam points beneath the rack.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: Hold on. What's in your filter?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Following the manual, Sam removes this model's filter. It has caught food debris from earlier meals.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: You were going to mention this when?

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: I... could use a cleaning.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Then we'll test the evidence instead of the attitude.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Poor loading isn't the only possible problem. This machine also needs care. And if cleaning stays poor after the recommended checks, a real fault may need investigation. A dirty bowl alone doesn't settle that.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Sam checks the manual, cleans the filter as directed, and locks it back in place. This time, food scraps go in the trash. Ordinary leftovers don't get a full sink wash. Stubborn or starchy messes get the pretreatment the manual calls for.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The bowls sit apart, with their insides facing the spray. Nothing obstructs the arms. Sam adds detergent made for dishwashers and chooses the appropriate cycle.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Court is in recess. Let the defendant work.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: After the cycle, Sam opens the door. The bowl comes out clean. The judge checks it against the original photo. Same bowl. A very different assignment.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: For this load, the complaint is dismissed.

lines.speaker: SAM
lines.text: So you actually can wash dishes?

lines.speaker: DISHWASHER
lines.text: It's literally my name.
